disqualifying_errors: Treating criteria and constraints as interchangeable.

Revising the criteria after testing so a preferred solution wins.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Weighted decision matrices and formal optimisation are later work.

A solution that violates a constraint has not solved the problem, however well it scores on the criteria.

The particle model explains why matter that seems to disappear, such as evaporating water or dissolving sugar, has not stopped existing.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming dissolving destroys the dissolved substance.
Claiming a mixture cannot be separated because it looks uniform.
Claiming any combination of substances is a new substance.
fixed_facts: In a mixture, the substances keep their own properties and can in principle be separated.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Solubility curves, concentration units, and the compound-versus-mixture distinction in chemical terms are Grade 7 and later work.
relationships: A mixture contains two or more substances that keep their own properties.
Mixtures can be separated by physical means such as filtering, sieving, evaporating, or using a magnet, because the substances have not been changed.
A substance that has dissolved is still present in the mixture, and evaporating the liquid recovers it.

disqualifying_errors: Reporting a measurement to more places than the tool can resolve.
Claiming precise measurements must be accurate.
Discarding a value that disagrees, without recording that it was discarded and why.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Significant figures, standard deviation, and formal uncertainty are Grade 7 and later work.

Repeating a measurement and getting similar values shows the method is reproducible.
Precision is about how closely repeated measurements agree; being close together is not the same as being right.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming groundwater flows in underground rivers everywhere beneath the surface.
Claiming surface water and groundwater are separate supplies that never mix.
Claiming pollution at the surface cannot reach groundwater.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Hydraulic conductivity, aquifer modelling, and recharge rates are High School work.
relationships: Water at the surface collects in streams, rivers, lakes, and wetlands, and water underground fills spaces between soil particles and cracks in rock.
Surface water and groundwater are connected: water moves between them, so what happens to one affects the other.
Water moves downhill at the surface and moves through the ground much more slowly than it moves in a river.

analysis_questions.prompt: Find a mistake in your earlier work on scientific argument — yours or one in an example. Say what the mistake was, then try the same kind of problem a different way: a drawing instead of numbers, or a model instead of words. Show that the new way gets it right.

Show what you found about scientific argument in the clearest way for this task — a labelled drawing, a table, a written explanation, or the steps you followed. Then say why you picked that way instead of just writing one sentence.
Find one place where you checked your work about scientific argument and changed something. Write what you changed, what made you notice it, and why the new version is better — not just different.

Answer the big question for this unit in two or three sentences, using scientific argument as your example: How can understanding integrated science and engineering capstone help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
Which one piece of evidence in your record best supports what you decided about scientific argument? Say what makes it good evidence, and name one thing that would make it even stronger.
Name one thing your work on scientific argument cannot tell you, even if you did everything carefully. Then say what someone would have to do differently to find that out.

Go through every number and observation in your record. For each one, write where it came from: you measured it, you worked it out, or it was given to you. Anything given to you is marked SUPPLIED with the name of the source and the date you looked it up.
